title: Adoption recognises a running sandbox instead of dispatching a rival
description:
This is the property that decides whether the executor is safe to restart into, and it is the one most likely to be quietly wrong.

A restarted orchestrator re-derives its state from git and reaches a tick that already has a sandbox running its attempt. It must ADOPT that sandbox by identity, not dispatch a second one. Two sandboxes on one tick means two workers pushing to one branch, which is the failure adoption-by-identity exists to prevent and which nothing downstream would cleanly recover from.

The existing mechanism is adoption by identity - w1c is the tick that fixed it picking the FIRST attempt of a tick rather than the latest, so read that before assuming the local rules transfer. What is new here is that the evidence of a live attempt is now on the other side of an HTTP boundary, and 'absent' from that route must be distinguishable from 'the route could not be reached'. Treating an unreachable factory as 'no sandbox running' is how a rival gets dispatched.

Axiom 1 applies with full force: cold reconstruction from git must reach the same dispatch decision as the process that is still warm.
notes: 2026-09-23 01:47 - ticfac run epic-xte: attempt 6 merged into epic/xte as 33a17fdcb630; the integrated gate (go, ts) passed.
acceptance_criteria: An orchestrator restarted mid-attempt adopts the running sandbox rather than starting a second, proven by a test that kills and re-derives; an unreachable factory is NOT treated as no-sandbox-running and does not dispatch; and go test -short ./... passes
